weir-head-from-flow.formula: 90-degree V-notch: H = (Q/C)^(1/2.48), C=2.49. Suppressed rectangular: H = (Q/(C L))^(2/3), C=3.33. Contracted rectangular: L-0.2H solved by fixed-point from the suppressed seed. 1 cfs = 448.831 GPM.
weir-head-from-flow.edition: Per the USBR Water Measurement Manual (public domain) - the V-notch and Francis rectangular-weir equations solved for the head, the inverse of the weir-flow tile, by name.
weir-head-from-flow.freeAccess: Free at usbr.gov/tsc/techreferences/mands/wmm; the user confirms the calibrated weir coefficient.
weir-head-from-flow.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
weir-head-from-flow.editionNote: The head over a sharp-crested weir needed to pass a target flow, the inverse of the weir-flow tile: a 90-degree V-notch inverts in closed form to H = (Q/C)^(1/2.48), a suppressed rectangular weir to H = (Q/(C L))^(2/3), and a contracted rectangular weir is solved by a few fixed-point passes because its effective crest length L - 0.2 H depends on the head. This sizes a weir box or sets a staff-gauge mark for a design flow. Requires a sharp-crested, ventilated, free-flow weir; a submerged/drowned condition is invalid, and a head below ~0.2 ft is a low-accuracy reading (flagged). An operations aid; the operator of record and the primacy agency govern compliance.

assumptions.name: Weir condition
assumptions.value: sharp-crested, ventilated, free-flow; fully contracted, or suppressed for the suppressed option

assumptions.name: Contracted solve
assumptions.value: the contracted weir's L - 0.2 H is solved by fixed-point iteration seeded from the suppressed form

growing-degree-days.formula: GDD = ((min(Tmax,cutoff) + Tmin_adj)/2) - base, floored at 0. The modified method caps Tmax at the cutoff and floors Tmin at the base before averaging.
growing-degree-days.edition: Per the USDA / NWS growing-degree-day method and McMaster & Wilhelm (1997), 'Growing degree-days: one equation, two interpretations,' Agric. & Forest Meteorology 87, by name.
growing-degree-days.freeAccess: Free at university extension sites and agresearch indexes; corn 50/86 F is the land-grant convention.
growing-degree-days.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
growing-degree-days.editionNote: Two methods (standard vs. modified); with the cutoff entered as its own field both cap Tmax, so they diverge on cold nights (the modified method floors Tmin at the base). The method is labeled. Days with Tmin > Tmax are skipped.

assumptions.name: Base/cutoff
assumptions.value: crop-specific (corn 50/86 F); user-supplied

sous-vide-pasteurization.formula: come_up_seconds = 2.245 * L_m^2 / alpha (one-term slab centerline solution, Fo for a 99.5% approach). hold_minutes from linear interpolation of FDA Food Code 3-401.11(B)(2) Table 3-2 (whole meat roasts) at the bath temperature. total = come_up + hold.
sous-vide-pasteurization.edition: FDA Food Code 3-401.11(B)(2) Table 3-2 (holding times for whole meat roasts). One-term slab thermal-diffusion solution.
sous-vide-pasteurization.freeAccess: fda.gov (Food, Retail Food Protection, FDA Food Code).
sous-vide-pasteurization.governance: The thermometer on the food is the verdict. Local health department governs.
sous-vide-pasteurization.editionNote: Field thermometer at the geometric center is the verdict. Other pathogens may require different times.

assumptions.name: Diffusivity values
assumptions.value: poultry / pork 1.4e-7; beef 1.3e-7; fish 1.45e-7; egg 1.4e-7 (m^2/s)

assumptions.name: Slab model
assumptions.value: half-thickness L = thickness / 2 (heat from both sides)
assumptions.source: engineering practice for sous-vide bag in bath

assumptions.name: Hold-time interpolation

assumptions.name: Limitation

hip-valley-rafter.formula: Common-rafter run multiplier m = sqrt(P² + 144) / 12 (P = pitch, rise per 12 in run). Hip / valley multiplier m_hip = sqrt(P² + 288) / 12 (square 12 × 12 diagonal = 16.97). Hip jacks: the n-th jack sits n × oc along the plate from the corner and runs that far to the hip, so its length is n × oc × m_common, each jack longer by the common difference oc × m_common (NAVEDTRA 14044: 19.23 in at 16 in o.c. and 8 in rise).
hip-valley-rafter.edition: Carpentry framing-square method by name. Public layout taught in any framing-square reference (Steel Square Pocket Book, Audel's Carpenters and Builders Library) by name.
hip-valley-rafter.freeAccess: Older Steel Square Pocket Book editions free at archive.org.

tankless-gpm.formula: Delivered heat (BTU/hr) = 8.33 × ΔT × GPM × 60 = rated input × thermal efficiency. Solved for GPM, required input, or temperature rise.
tankless-gpm.edition: ASHRAE Handbook (HVAC Systems and Equipment) by name; manufacturer ratings on the heater nameplate.
tankless-gpm.freeAccess: ASHRAE Handbook licensed; manufacturer data sheets free at each manufacturer site.
tankless-gpm.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.

assumptions.value: 8.33 (BTU per gal-°F)

hydronic-fill-pressure.formula: static = height / 2.31; fill = static + margin; 2.31 ft of water column = 1 psi; margin (~4 psi) keeps the top of the loop above atmospheric.
hydronic-fill-pressure.edition: Hydronic fill-pressure by static height, standard heating-system practice (ASHRAE Handbook, HVAC Systems and Equipment; boiler manufacturer instructions) by name.
hydronic-fill-pressure.freeAccess: The height / 2.31 static-head conversion is public physics; the boiler and fill-valve settings are manufacturer data.
hydronic-fill-pressure.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed plumber / gas fitter govern. Verify against the IPC / IFGC edition adopted in your jurisdiction.
hydronic-fill-pressure.editionNote: The cold-fill (make-up) pressure of a closed hydronic loop must lift water to the highest point plus a small margin so the top stays above atmospheric, which prevents air from being drawn in and keeps the circulator from cavitating: fill = height / 2.31 + margin, where 2.31 ft of water column equals 1 psi. The margin, the pressure remaining at the top, is commonly about 4 psi (JMPCO; some designers hold an 8 psig minimum fill, RL Deppmann). Set the automatic fill valve and match the expansion-tank pre-charge to this pressure; the relief valve (typically 30 psi on a residential boiler) must sit well above it. A design aid; the boiler and system manufacturer's instructions govern.

assumptions.name: Static head
assumptions.value: static = height / 2.31 (2.31 ft of water = 1 psi)

assumptions.name: Top margin
assumptions.value: add ~4 psi so the top of the system stays above atmospheric

assumptions.name: Manufacturer governs
assumptions.value: the boiler's fill and relief settings and the expansion-tank pre-charge govern

deck-beam-post.formula: Tributary width to beam = joist span / 2; beam load w (plf) = (live + dead) psf × tributary. Smallest built-up beam with min(L_bending, L_deflection) ≥ post spacing. Post axial load = w × post spacing; NDS column capacity = F_c × C_P × A with C_P from F_cE = 0.822 E_min / (le/d)². Footing from soil bearing; ledger fastener spacing from IRC Table R507.9.1.3(1).
deck-beam-post.edition: IRC 2021 (International Residential Code). §R507 (decks). AWC NDS-2018 (National Design Specification for Wood Construction). reference values; IRC Table R507.9.1.3(1) ledger fasteners.
deck-beam-post.freeAccess: Free read-only access at codes.iccsafe.org. AWC NDS free at awc.org.
deck-beam-post.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed structural engineer govern.
deck-beam-post.editionNote: Editions available: bundled values follow IRC 2021. Jurisdictions on IRC 2018 / 2024 differ at the margins; verify the edition adopted by your AHJ.

assumptions.name: Deck loads
assumptions.value: 40 psf live + 10 psf dead per IRC R507 default

assumptions.name: Column stability
assumptions.value: pinned-pinned (K_e = 1), c = 0.8 for sawn lumber, E_min and F_c for the 4x4 from NDS Supplement Table 4A/4B No.2 dimension lumber and for the 6x6 from Table 4D No.2 Posts and Timbers (5x5 and larger)

assumptions.name: Ledger schedule
assumptions.value: 1/2 in lag / approved fastener spacing by joist span, attached decks only

windrow-stockpile-volume.formula: radius = width/2; height = radius x tan(repose x pi/180); cross_section = 1/2 x width x height; volume = cross_section x ridge_length + (1/3) pi radius^2 height; volume_cy = volume/27; tons = volume x density/2000.
windrow-stockpile-volume.edition: Elongated-stockpile geometry by name - a triangular prism (the straight ridge run) plus one full cone across the two tapered ends; first-principles geometry with the angle-of-repose relation.
windrow-stockpile-volume.freeAccess: The prism, cone, and angle-of-repose relations are public geometry and soil-mechanics practice.
windrow-stockpile-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
windrow-stockpile-volume.editionNote: An elongated stockpile - a windrow dumped or graded along a line - modeled as a triangular prism with the two tapered ends together making one full cone; height = (width/2) tan(repose). Set the ridge length to 0 and it collapses to the conical stockpile-volume pile. The angle of repose depends on the material and its moisture (roughly 30-40 degrees for granular material) and steepens as the material gets damp or angular; an irregular base, a flat (bulldozed) top, or a pile pushed against a wall all change it. A survey volume governs for payment.

assumptions.name: Shape
assumptions.value: triangular prism (ridge run) + one full cone at the ends; ridge length 0 gives the conical pile

assumptions.name: Angle of repose
assumptions.value: 37 degrees default (granular material runs ~30-40 degrees); moisture and angularity steepen it

assumptions.name: Bulk density
assumptions.value: 100 pcf default loose (the material governs); a survey governs for payment

weld-usage.formula: Deposit weight = section_area × length × 0.283 lb/in³ (steel). Consumable weight = deposit / efficiency. Efficiency by process: SMAW 60%, GMAW 90%, FCAW 80%, GTAW 100%.
weld-usage.edition: AWS Welding Handbook by name; AWS A5 series filler-metal specifications by name.
weld-usage.freeAccess: AWS A5 specs licensed; AWS outreach materials free at aws.org.

mold.edition: EPA 402-K-01-001 (Mold Remediation in Schools and Commercial Buildings) + IICRC S520-2024 (Standard for Professional Mold Remediation) by name.

air-sample-volume.formula: run_time_min = target_volume_L / flow_rate_lpm; run_time_sec = run_time_min * 60; total_volume_L = target_volume_L * sample_count; total_time_min = run_time_min * sample_count (sequential on one pump).
air-sample-volume.edition: ASTM D7391 (spore-trap method) and the cassette manufacturer's instructions; AIHA-accredited laboratory analysis.
air-sample-volume.freeAccess: ASTM D7391 licensed; cassette manufacturer instructions free with the product. AIHA lab accreditation directory free at aiha.org.
air-sample-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
air-sample-volume.editionNote: The calibrated rotameter flow governs (not the nominal pump rating); the cassette manufacturer sets the acceptable volume window. The worked example uses spore-trap placeholders (15 L/min, 75 L); there is no default.

assumptions.name: Spore-trap example values
assumptions.value: 15 L/min flow, 75 L target volume

nfa-fireground-flow.formula: base = (length x width / 3) x (percent_involved / 100) x floors_involved; exposure = 0.25 x base per exposure; total = base + exposure; valid when percent_involved <= 50 and base <= 1000 gpm.
nfa-fireground-flow.edition: National Fire Academy fireground fire-flow quick-calc (NFA; IFSTA), by name.
nfa-fireground-flow.freeAccess: The NFA quick-calc is public fire-service training material; incident command governs the actual attack.
nfa-fireground-flow.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed fire protection engineer govern.
nfa-fireground-flow.editionNote: The formula is validated only for interior/offensive attack up to about 50% involvement and roughly 1,000 gpm - beyond that it under-predicts badly and the fight is defensive (use the ISO / required-fire-flow method); it is a mental scene-size-up tool, not a water-supply design. A size-up aid, not a water-supply design.

assumptions.name: Validity envelope
assumptions.value: interior/offensive attack, <= 50% involvement, <= ~1,000 gpm base; outside it the fire is defensive

assumptions.name: Additions
assumptions.value: 0.25 x base per exposure; multiply the base by the number of involved floors

line-array-splay.formula: dh = trim_height_ft - ear_height_ft; angle_near = atan(dh / near_throw_ft); angle_far = atan(dh / far_throw_ft); coverage = angle_near - angle_far; avg_splay = coverage / cabinets; level_taper_db = 20 log10(far_throw / near_throw).
line-array-splay.edition: Line-array vertical coverage from the trim geometry with the inverse-square (20 log) level taper between the near and far rows, by name; a design starting point, and the manufacturer's prediction software and the array's mechanical splay limits govern the rig.
line-array-splay.freeAccess: The coverage angle is trigonometry on the trim height and the two throws, and the taper is the inverse-square law. All five inputs are the rig's own dimensions.
line-array-splay.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
line-array-splay.editionNote: An array hung at a trim height has to cover the angle between the down-tilt to the first row and the down-tilt to the last, and that angle is fixed by geometry rather than by the boxes: it is the arctangent of the drop over the near throw, less the arctangent of the same drop over the far throw, where the drop is the trim height above the listeners' ears. Dividing the covered angle by the cabinet count gives the average splay, which is the design starting point a manufacturer's prediction software then refines against real cabinet directivity. The level-taper line explains why the splays are never actually equal in a finished design. The last row is far more distant than the first and therefore much quieter by inverse square, and the array recovers that by aiming more of its energy at the far seats: tight splays at the top of the array where the boxes throw long, opening toward the bottom where the boxes cover the near rows. The taper figure states how much level the splay pattern is being asked to make up, and a large taper across a shallow coverage angle means the top boxes will sit at the array's minimum mechanical splay while the bottom ones open several degrees. A higher trim or a shorter room reduces the asymmetry the same cabinets have to produce. This is where a design starts, not where it ends.

assumptions.name: Coverage is geometric
assumptions.value: the angle to cover is set by trim height and the two throws, not by the loudspeaker

assumptions.name: Taper drives asymmetry
assumptions.value: 20 log(far/near) is the level the splay pattern must recover, so splays tighten at the top and open at the bottom
assumptions.source: inverse-square law applied to array design

assumptions.name: Starting point only
assumptions.value: the manufacturer's prediction software and the array's mechanical splay limits govern the rig

estimated-tax.formula: Required annual payment = min(0.90 * projected_current_tax, multiplier * prior_year_tax). multiplier = 1.10 if prior-year AGI > $150k else 1.00. After-withholding = required - withholding. Per-quarter = after-withholding / 4.
estimated-tax.edition: IRC 6654 (failure-to-pay-estimated-tax safe harbors). IRS Form 1040-ES quarterly schedule.
estimated-tax.freeAccess: Free at irs.gov/forms-pubs/about-form-1040-es. Due dates bundled per year in ESTIMATED_TAX_DUE_DATES.
estimated-tax.governance: Estimate only. Tax law changes. Confirm with the current IRS publication or a licensed CPA before filing.
estimated-tax.editionNote: Annual cadence: due dates roll forward each year, with statutory weekend / holiday rollover applied by the IRS.

assumptions.name: Safe harbor
assumptions.value: smaller of 90% current-year or 100% / 110% prior-year tax

assumptions.name: Equal installments
assumptions.value: even quarterly split (the annualized-income alternative is not modeled)
assumptions.source: user choice; Form 2210 covers the alternative

per-diem-interest.formula: daily_interest = loan_amount * (annual_rate/100) / basis (365, 360, or 30/360). days_to_eom = last_day_of_month - closing_day + 1 (counting the closing day; 30/360 uses 30 - min(closing_day, 30) + 1, so a close on the 31st accrues one day). prepaid_interest = daily_interest * days_to_eom.
per-diem-interest.edition: CFPB Closing Disclosure (12 CFR 1026.38, Appendix H) prepaid-interest line item.
per-diem-interest.freeAccess: Closing Disclosure form and Regulation Z free at consumerfinance.gov and ecfr.gov.
per-diem-interest.governance: Estimate. Lender governs final underwriting and rate / fee disclosure. Appraiser governs the appraised value. State law and the agency's program guidelines may impose stricter limits than the published thresholds.
per-diem-interest.editionNote: Prepaid (odd-days) interest covers the stub period from closing through the end of the month, because the first regular payment is due the first of the following month and pays in arrears. The day-count convention varies by lender; Actual/365 is typical for owner-occupied conventional loans. Lender governs the actual figure.

assumptions.name: Stub period
assumptions.value: closing day through the last day of the closing month, inclusive

assumptions.name: Day-count basis
assumptions.value: 365, 360, or 30/360 per the selected convention

sump-basin-sizing.formula: area_ft2 = (PI/4)(basin_dia/12)^2; drawdown_gal = area_ft2 x (drawdown_in/12) x 7.48; run_time_s = drawdown_gal / (pump_gpm - inflow_gpm) x 60; fill_time_s = drawdown_gal / inflow_gpm x 60; cycles_per_hr = 3600 / (run + fill); adequate = run_time_s >= min_run_s; optional sewage discharge check against IPC Table 712.4.2 (2 in 21 gpm, 2-1/2 in 30 gpm, 3 in 46 gpm) with velocity = gpm / (448.83 x (PI/4)(d/12)^2), 448.83 = 60 x 1728/231.
sump-basin-sizing.edition: IPC 2021 Section 712 (Sumps and Ejectors) and the Hydraulic Institute pump-cycling guidance by name; first-principles basin geometry and cycle math.
sump-basin-sizing.freeAccess: IPC 2021 free read-only at codes.iccsafe.org; the 7.48 gal/ft^3 constant is public.
sump-basin-sizing.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
sump-basin-sizing.editionNote: The pump must out-pace the inflow (the tile errors if it does not). A longer run time per cycle is gentler on the motor. A sewage ejector must pass 2 in solids and carries a vent, neither of which this tile sizes (IPC 712.3-712.4); the optional discharge-size select checks the IPC Table 712.4.2 minimum capacity.

assumptions.name: Volume constant
assumptions.value: 7.48 gal per ft^3

assumptions.name: Minimum run default
assumptions.value: 60 s per cycle (Hydraulic Institute cycling guidance)

assumptions.name: Ejector minimum capacity
assumptions.value: 21 / 30 / 46 gpm for a 2 / 2-1/2 / 3 in discharge, each about 2 ft/s in that pipe (added 2026-10-09)

riprap-d50.formula: d50_ft = safety_factor x velocity_fps^2 / (2 x 32.2 x turbulence_coeff^2 x (specific_gravity - 1)); d50_in = d50_ft x 12.
riprap-d50.edition: Isbash riprap-sizing equation by name (public-domain field estimate); first-principles unit arithmetic (g = 32.2 ft/s^2).
riprap-d50.freeAccess: The Isbash equation is public-domain; every input is user-entered (no gradation table or design chart reproduced).
riprap-d50.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
riprap-d50.editionNote: The turbulence coefficient C is about 0.86 for high-turbulence zones (below outlets, at bends) and about 1.20 for low-turbulence straight channels - it enters squared, so it moves the answer as much as velocity. Isbash is a public-domain field estimate; the hydraulic engineer and the AHJ govern the channel design. The layer thickness (at least 1.5 x D50) and the gradation are taken off separately.

assumptions.name: Turbulence coefficient
assumptions.value: C ~ 0.86 high-turbulence (below outlets, bends), ~1.20 low-turbulence (straight channels)

assumptions.name: Stone specific gravity
assumptions.value: 2.65 default (typical quarried stone); the stone source governs

assumptions.name: Safety factor
assumptions.value: default 1.2 applied to D50; the published Isbash equation (NRCS TS14C) carries none, so enter 1 to reproduce it

stucco-coverage.edition: Portland-cement plaster bag-count identity by name (volume in square-foot-inches over the bag yield, plus waste); first-principles arithmetic.

The bag yield is the product's coverage at a reference thickness (square-foot-inches per bag). The sand and lime are batched per the mix design. Distinct from the masonry mortar-mix and thinset-coverage.

assumptions.name: Coat thickness

assumptions.name: Bag yield
assumptions.value: ~10.1 square-foot-inches per 80-lb bag (default); the product sets it

anchor-epoxy-volume.formula: per_hole_in3 = (PI/4) x (hole_dia_in^2 - bar_dia_in^2) x embed_in; total_in3 = holes x per_hole_in3 x (1 + waste_pct/100); cartridges = ceil(total_in3 / cartridge_in3).
anchor-epoxy-volume.edition: Adhesive-anchor epoxy-volume identity by name (annular fill per hole, times the holes, over the cartridge volume); first-principles geometry.
anchor-epoxy-volume.freeAccess: The annular-volume geometry is public first-principles; the hole diameter comes from the adhesive manufacturer's printed installation instructions.
anchor-epoxy-volume.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
anchor-epoxy-volume.editionNote: This is the annular fill between the bar and the hole. The hole diameter comes from the adhesive manufacturer's printed installation instructions (oversized relative to the bar). The waste covers the mixing-nozzle purge at each cartridge start. Distinct from the concrete-anchor capacity calcs.

assumptions.name: Hole diameter
assumptions.value: from the adhesive manufacturer's MPII, oversized relative to the bar (e.g. 3/4 in hole for a 5/8 in bar)

assumptions.name: Waste
assumptions.value: ~10% for the mixing-nozzle purge at each cartridge start

circular-arc-rise-from-radius.formula: Rise = R - sqrt(R^2 - (chord/2)^2), the inverse of R = (chord^2/4 + rise^2)/(2 rise); central angle = 2 x asin((chord/2)/R); arc length = R x angle. The chord cannot exceed the diameter (R >= chord/2).
circular-arc-rise-from-radius.edition: Circular arc from a chord and radius (the sagitta / middle-ordinate relation) - first-principles circle geometry as in Machinery's Handbook (Industrial Press), by name; public domain.
circular-arc-rise-from-radius.freeAccess: Pure circle geometry, public; the chord and radius are user-supplied.
circular-arc-rise-from-radius.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
circular-arc-rise-from-radius.editionNote: First-principles geometry solved for the rise: the perpendicular height of the MINOR arc at midspan (the sagitta / middle ordinate) from a known radius and chord. The chord cannot exceed the diameter (the radius must be at least half the chord); at the diameter the rise equals the radius (a semicircle). Reproduce the curve by swinging the radius from the center, or offset the rise up from the chord midpoint and half the chord to each end, then trammel/string-line at the radius.

assumptions.name: Chord and radius
assumptions.value: the chord (span) and the radius are user-supplied; rise = R - sqrt(R^2 - (chord/2)^2)

assumptions.name: Minor arc
assumptions.value: returns the minor-arc rise; the chord must be no longer than the diameter

retaining-wall-block.formula: Buried = max(1 in/ft of height, one block height); courses = ceil(total height / block height); total = courses x ceil(run x 12 / block length); gravel by zone geometry.
retaining-wall-block.edition: Segmental retaining-wall maker guidance (Allan Block / Versa-Lok, by name).
retaining-wall-block.freeAccess: Install guides free at the block maker's pages.
retaining-wall-block.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
retaining-wall-block.editionNote: Single-edition (engineering-practice / first-principles take-off; refresh as practice and product data shift).

assumptions.value: bury ~1 in per ft, 2 ft x 6 in base pad, 12 in drainage zone (fixed in the take-off); engineered design over ~4 ft

refrigerant-leak-rate.formula: annualizing: leak_rate_pct = pounds of one addition / full_charge_lb x (12 / months since the previous addition) x 100; rolling average: leak_rate_pct = pounds added over the previous 365 days / full_charge_lb x 100 (no scaling); allowed_lb = the threshold's pounds for the same window; exceeded when the rate is above the threshold.
refrigerant-leak-rate.edition: The annualized leak-rate calculation of 40 CFR Part 82 Subpart F (ozone-depleting refrigerants, 50 lb and up) and, from January 1, 2026, 40 CFR 84.106 (HFCs at any GWP and substitutes with GWP above 53, 15 lb and up, excluding residential and light commercial AC and heat pumps) -- pounds added divided by the FULL CHARGE, by the 82.152 annualizing or rolling-average method, against the threshold for the appliance type -- cited by part and not reproduced. The thresholds differ by appliance category and are entered rather than bundled. 40 CFR Part 82 in full, the appliance's category, and the service records govern.
refrigerant-leak-rate.freeAccess: The calculation is public federal regulation stated as a relation and cited by part; the full charge, pounds added, period, and applicable threshold are the owner's own records.
refrigerant-leak-rate.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
refrigerant-leak-rate.editionNote: The rule is simple arithmetic with real teeth. For an appliance containing fifty pounds or more of refrigerant, the owner or operator tracks refrigerant added, annualizes it against the full charge -- the amount the system is designed to hold, not what happens to be in it -- and compares the result against the threshold for that appliance type, which differs by category, with commercial and industrial process refrigeration at higher percentages than comfort cooling and other appliances. Two details cause most of the errors. Full charge must be established and documented, and a system whose full charge has never been recorded cannot compute a compliant leak rate at all, which makes the recordkeeping a precondition rather than a formality. And there are two permitted methods: the annualizing method scales one addition by 12 over the months since the previous addition, so the same 34 lb on a 200 lb system reads 17% over twelve months but 34% six months after the previous top-off, while the rolling-average method sums the previous 365 days and does not scale a shorter window. Identifying the appliance category correctly is the first step, because the same quantity of refrigerant is a violation on one category and well inside the allowance on another. Exceeding the threshold starts a clock: leak repairs within a set number of days, verification tests, and, if the leak cannot be repaired, a retrofit or retirement plan.

assumptions.name: Full charge
assumptions.value: the design charge, documented; without it no compliant leak rate can be computed

assumptions.name: Two methods
assumptions.value: annualizing scales one addition by 12 / months since the previous one; rolling average sums 365 days and does not scale; one method for every appliance at a facility

assumptions.name: HFC scope
assumptions.value: from 2026, 15 lb or more of an HFC (any GWP) or a substitute over GWP 53; residential and light commercial AC and heat pumps are excluded

assumptions.name: Threshold by category
assumptions.value: differs by appliance type and is entered, not bundled; the same pounds can be a violation on one and not another

degree-of-curve.formula: chord definition D = 2 arcsin(50 / R), R = 50 / sin(D / 2); arc definition R = 18,000 / pi / D; middle ordinate M = R (1 - cos(theta / 2)) with theta = 2 arcsin(chord / (2 R)); curve length = 100 x central angle / D.
degree-of-curve.edition: The chord and arc definitions of degree of curve and the middle-ordinate relation, by name, with the 62 ft chord field rule; 49 CFR 213 named for the alignment limits this does not evaluate. First-principles curve trigonometry. The railroad's engineering instructions and the track owner govern.
degree-of-curve.freeAccess: Plane trigonometry on the user's own curve; no proprietary table is reproduced.
degree-of-curve.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
degree-of-curve.editionNote: A one degree curve turns one degree over a hundred-foot chord, and the useful field consequence is the 62 ft chord rule: the middle ordinate of a 62 ft chord, measured in inches, is very nearly the degree of curve. That is a measurement a track inspector can make with a string and a rule, standing on the track, with no instrument, which is exactly the kind of arithmetic worth carrying. The chord-versus-arc distinction is small on flat curves and grows as they sharpen. At one degree the two definitions differ by well under a foot of radius; by ten or twelve degrees the gap is meaningful, and a radius handed between a railroad and a highway designer without stating the definition can be wrong by enough to matter at a grade crossing or a clearance check. Middle ordinate is the other everyday number, because string-lining a curve to find where it needs to move is still done with a chord and a ruler on a great deal of track. What that does NOT amount to is an alignment evaluation: string-lining for real takes a series of ordinates along the curve rather than one, and the throws needed to correct alignment are a separate exercise.

assumptions.name: Chord and arc are different definitions
assumptions.value: the gap grows with the sharpness of the curve and must be stated when a radius changes hands

assumptions.name: The 62 ft chord rule
assumptions.value: middle ordinate in inches is very nearly the degree of curve; a string-and-rule measurement

assumptions.name: One ordinate is not an alignment check
assumptions.value: string-lining takes a series of ordinates along the curve

slope-stability-infinite.formula: driving = gamma H sin(beta) cos(beta); resisting = c' + gamma H cos^2(beta) tan(phi'); FS = resisting / driving. (c' = 0 collapses to FS = tan(phi')/tan(beta))
slope-stability-infinite.edition: The infinite-slope stability model -- the factor of safety of a shallow translational slide on a plane parallel to a long uniform slope, with its cohesionless reduction tan(phi')/tan(beta) -- as compiled in Das (Principles of Geotechnical Engineering) and the NAVFAC DM-7 slope-stability references, by name.
slope-stability-infinite.freeAccess: NAVFAC DM-7 is public-domain and free online; the infinite-slope relations are public in the standard geotechnical texts.
slope-stability-infinite.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
slope-stability-infinite.editionNote: The infinite-slope factor of safety FS = (c' + gamma H cos^2(beta) tan(phi')) / (gamma H sin(beta) cos(beta)) and its cohesionless reduction FS = tan(phi')/tan(beta), as compiled in the Das and NAVFAC slope-stability references. This returns the factor of safety against a shallow translational slide on a plane parallel to a long, uniform slope with no seepage (dry, or water table below the failure plane) - it is not a circular/rotational (Bishop/Spencer) analysis, assumes a uniform soil and an infinite slope (edge effects and finite geometry ignored), takes drained effective-stress parameters, and excludes pore pressure / steady seepage (the gamma - gamma_w submerged case is a follow-on) and seismic loading. A design/screening aid, not a substitute for a geotechnical engineer's stability analysis.

assumptions.name: Failure mode
assumptions.value: a shallow translational slide parallel to the surface at depth H; strength-over-stress ratio

assumptions.name: Cohesionless case
assumptions.value: c' = 0 gives FS = tan(phi')/tan(beta), independent of depth and unit weight (the angle of repose at FS = 1)

assumptions.name: No seepage
assumptions.value: dry slope or water table below the plane; steady-seepage and seismic cases are separate

taping-normal-tension.formula: set the tension correction equal and opposite to the sag correction, (P - P0) L / (A E) = w^2 L^3 / (24 P^2); substituting the span weight W = w L eliminates L and gives P^2 (P - P0) = A E W^2 / 24, solved by bisection. Square-rooting the same relation gives the textbook implicit form P = 0.204 W sqrt(A E) / sqrt(P - P0), where 0.204 = 1/sqrt(24).
taping-normal-tension.edition: Normal tension as defined in the standard surveying references (Ghilani/Wolf, Elementary Surveying), by name. The component corrections are the same tension and sag expressions the taping-corrections tile uses, so the two tiles cannot drift.
taping-normal-tension.freeAccess: Both corrections and the normal-tension condition are elementary mechanics published in every surveying text and in free course notes; nothing here is tabulated or proprietary.
taping-normal-tension.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
taping-normal-tension.editionNote: The derivation is the interesting part and it is fully shown rather than asserted: pulling harder stretches the tape (a positive correction that grows linearly with P) while the tape's own weight sags the span (a negative correction that shrinks as 1/P^2), so exactly one pull makes them cancel. Writing the span weight as W = w L removes the length from both sides entirely, which is why normal tension depends on the tape and the span weight but not separately on how long the span is. The cubic is solved directly by bisection; the classic 0.204 constant is not a fitted coefficient but 1 over the square root of 24, and the fuzzer checks the bisection root against that closed form rather than against a memorized value. Practical limits are stated in the note: normal tension can exceed what a crew holds steadily or what the tape is rated for, a tape supported throughout has no sag to cancel, and cancelling these two corrections does nothing about temperature or the tape's own standardization error - those still need the taping-corrections tile. Steel modulus 29,000,000 psi by default; the tape's actual cross-sectional area and weight per foot come from its specification and move the answer substantially. A field aid; the tape calibration and the survey's procedure govern.

assumptions.name: Cancellation condition
assumptions.value: tension correction = -(sag correction) at the normal tension

assumptions.name: Governing equation
assumptions.value: P^2 (P - P0) = A E W^2 / 24, length-independent once W = w L
assumptions.source: derived from the two correction formulas

assumptions.name: 0.204 constant
assumptions.value: 1/sqrt(24) = 0.20412, derived rather than fitted

assumptions.name: Steel modulus
assumptions.value: 29,000,000 psi default, editable

assumptions.name: Scope
assumptions.value: does not address temperature or standardization error; may exceed a practical or rated pull

hydronic-gpm-deltat.formula: Q_btuh = (unit == tons) ? load x 12,000 : load; GPM = Q_btuh / (factor x dT); chilled-water shortcut GPM = 24 tons/dT (water).
hydronic-gpm-deltat.edition: The water-side sensible-heat transport Q = 500 x GPM x dT and its rearrangement to the design flow, with the chilled-water 24 tons/dT shortcut and the glycol-lowered factor, a standard hydronic relation, by name.
hydronic-gpm-deltat.freeAccess: The water-side heat-transport equation and its 500 factor are public hydronic-design results.
hydronic-gpm-deltat.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
hydronic-gpm-deltat.editionNote: The hydronic flow GPM = Q / (500 dT) from Q = 500 GPM dT (500 = 8.33 lb/gal x 60 min/h x 1.0 Btu/lb-degF for water), the chilled-water form GPM = 24 tons/dT (12,000/500 = 24), and the note that a propylene-glycol mix lowers the 500 factor (468 to 476 at 30% PG by Dow's published properties; glycol-fluid-factor gives it) via its density and specific heat. This returns the design system flow for pure water at the sea-level factor - it uses 500 (adjust for glycol or a different fluid via the fluid factor), assumes the full load is carried by the entered delta-T (no bypass or primary/secondary decoupling), and does not size the pump head (pump-tdh does), the pipe, or the coil. A design aid, not a substitute for the mechanical engineer of record's design.

assumptions.name: Heat transport
assumptions.value: GPM = Q / (500 dT) for water; 500 = 8.33 x 60 x 1.0

assumptions.name: Fluid factor
assumptions.value: 468 at 40 F to 476 at 180 F for 30% propylene glycol by volume (until 2026-10-09 this said about 485); glycol-fluid-factor gives it for a concentration and temperature
assumptions.source: Dow DOWFROST HD typical properties, Form 180-01273-402AMS

category-deterioration.formula: Reference lookup with threshold comparisons: origin category + elapsed wet hours + warm flag + contaminant-contact flag -> likely current category. Contaminant contact -> Category 3; Category 1 at or past 48 h (24 h if warm) -> Category 2; Category 2 at or past 24 h when warm -> Category 3; otherwise origin.
category-deterioration.edition: Category-at-time-of-remediation principle, by name; ANSI/IICRC S500.
category-deterioration.freeAccess: Adds the time dimension to the water category: a clean loss left standing, warm, or in contact with contaminated materials degrades to a higher category.
category-deterioration.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
category-deterioration.editionNote: Single-edition (the S500 principle). Category is a PROFESSIONAL determination made at the time of restoration, not by the source alone; elevated temperature and contact with contaminated materials accelerate the shift. The amplification window commonly cited is on the order of 48-72 hours under favorable conditions. When in doubt the HIGHER category is assumed - the restorer and ANSI/IICRC S500 GOVERN.

assumptions.name: Amplification window
assumptions.value: commonly cited on the order of 48-72 hours under favorable conditions (sooner if warm)

assumptions.name: When in doubt
assumptions.value: assume the higher category

vibration-forcing-frequencies.formula: running speed 1x = rpm / 60 Hz; blade or vane pass = 1x x the blade count; gear mesh = 1x x the tooth count with sidebands spaced at 1x; belt frequency = 1x x pi x sheave diameter / belt length; twice line frequency = 2 x the supply frequency; rotor bar pass = 1x x the bar count.
vibration-forcing-frequencies.edition: The standard rotating-machinery forcing frequencies as condition monitoring practice, by name. Where to LOOK, not a diagnosis: amplitude, phase, axial content and resonance decide what a peak means. The machine and component manufacturers' data and a qualified vibration analyst govern any diagnosis.
vibration-forcing-frequencies.freeAccess: Multiplication of shaft speed by part counts the user supplies; no spectrum or manufacturer table is reproduced.
vibration-forcing-frequencies.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
vibration-forcing-frequencies.editionNote: Every rotating part announces itself at a frequency tied to shaft speed, so identifying a peak, dividing by running speed, and reading off the integer names the component. The classic confusions are what a technician actually gets wrong: unbalance is 1x and dominantly radial; misalignment is usually 2x with significant AXIAL energy, and it is the axial content rather than the frequency that separates the two in the field; looseness throws a picket fence of harmonics. And a peak at twice line frequency is ELECTRICAL no matter how much it looks like a shaft harmonic -- a genuine trap near 3,540 rpm, where 2x running is about 118 Hz against a 120 Hz supply and a spectrum alone cannot separate them. There the only reliable test is to cut power and watch whether the peak vanishes instantly, because an electrical line dies with the field while a mechanical one coasts down. Gear mesh sidebands are reported because their PRESENCE is the finding: a healthy mesh shows the line without them.

assumptions.name: Where to look, not what is wrong
assumptions.value: every one of these lines is present on a healthy machine

assumptions.name: Amplitude is not evaluated
assumptions.value: it is what separates a normal forcing frequency from a problem

assumptions.name: Resonance is not addressed
assumptions.value: it amplifies whatever excites it and can make a small forcing function dominate

guy-anchor-holding-capacity.formula: cohesive Q_u = A (9 c + gamma D); granular Q_u = A gamma D N_q; allowable = ultimate / factor of safety; screw-anchor torque correlation Q_u = K_t x T.
guy-anchor-holding-capacity.edition: The deep-anchor uplift bearing relations as standard practice, by name, with the empirical screw-anchor torque correlation reported alongside. Single helix, deep-failure assumption. The anchor manufacturer's data, a geotechnical evaluation of the actual site, the utility's construction standards, and the applicable NESC edition govern.
guy-anchor-holding-capacity.freeAccess: A bearing calculation on soil properties the user supplies; no manufacturer capacity table is reproduced.
guy-anchor-holding-capacity.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
guy-anchor-holding-capacity.editionNote: The guy-tension calculator gives the pull in the guy and nothing says whether the ground will hold it -- and an anchor that pulls is the failure mode that takes the pole with it. In clay the strength is dominated by cohesion and the depth term is small; in sand there is no cohesion and the whole capacity is overburden times a bearing factor that climbs steeply with friction angle. A 12 in helix at 7 ft holds 7,673 lb ultimate in a stiff clay at 1,000 psf and 6,048 lb in a loose sand at N_q = 10: same hardware, same depth, and the soil is the whole variable. For power-installed screw anchors the installing torque is the better number, because it measures the soil that is actually there rather than the soil someone guessed at from a boring two hundred feet away -- and where the two methods disagree by a wide margin THAT DISAGREEMENT IS THE FINDING. A shallow anchor fails by lifting a soil cone to the surface, which is a different and weaker mechanism this does not model.

assumptions.name: Deep-failure assumption
assumptions.value: a shallow anchor fails by a weaker cone mechanism not modelled here

assumptions.name: Single helix
assumptions.value: multiple helices and their spacing rules are not summed

assumptions.name: The torque factor is manufacturer-specific
assumptions.value: it is set by shaft size and is empirical

bill-disaggregation.formula: a two-parameter energy signature: annual consumption = baseload + slope x heating degree days at the fitted balance point; the weather-sensitive share is slope x degree days over the total, and the implied building UA is slope x equipment efficiency x BTU per unit / 24.
bill-disaggregation.edition: Degree-day regression of utility bills (the energy signature method) as ASHRAE Fundamentals and PRISM-style bill analysis describe it, with the baseload, slope and balance point ENTERED as fitted parameters rather than derived here. The regression itself is not performed by this calculation.
bill-disaggregation.freeAccess: One linear relation and one unit conversion.
bill-disaggregation.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
bill-disaggregation.editionNote: The split decides where the money goes: a bill that is mostly baseload will not respond to insulation however good the insulation is, and one that is mostly weather-sensitive will. The balance point is the parameter people get wrong -- it is FITTED, not the conventional 65 degF, and a well-insulated house with large internal gains balances materially lower; using the wrong base temperature makes both the intercept and the slope meaningless. The UA implied by the slope is worth comparing against a modelled one, because a large disagreement means one of the two is wrong.

assumptions.name: Baseload, slope and balance point are fitted parameters
assumptions.value: entered here, not regressed

assumptions.name: Degree days at the fitted base
assumptions.value: not the conventional 65 degF base

assumptions.name: Whole-building UA
assumptions.value: includes infiltration and duct losses, not a takeoff U-value

square-to-round-development.formula: true length of an element line = sqrt(plan distance squared + height squared); the developed curved edge is the sum of the chords across the elements, each chord being 2 R sin(pi / N) for N elements, which must come back to pi x diameter.
square-to-round-development.edition: Triangulation development of a square-to-round transition by name. Seam and lap allowances are added to the developed shape, not part of it. It gives the governing true lengths, the element chord, the circumference check and the sheet size; it does not emit pattern coordinates or develop an eccentric transition's unequal elements individually. SMACNA's duct construction standards, the shop's layout practice, and a test piece govern.
square-to-round-development.freeAccess: One hypotenuse and one sine on dimensions the reader has; no pattern or standard text is reproduced.
square-to-round-development.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
square-to-round-development.editionNote: Triangulation is the method and TRUE LENGTH is the only idea in it. Any line on a square-to-round that is neither vertical nor horizontal appears shorter in every orthogonal view than it really is, so laying out from plan dimensions produces a pattern too small and a fitting that will not close. The circle is divided into elements because a curve cannot be triangulated directly, and each element develops as a straight chord -- so the developed edge is an inscribed polygon and always SHORT of the true circumference. More elements close that gap and cost layout time, and the shortfall at the entered count is reported so the choice is made with a number. The check at the end is worth doing every time: finding an error on the bench costs a sheet, finding it at the fitting costs the fitting.

assumptions.name: A concentric transition's governing elements
assumptions.value: an offset makes every element different and needs all of them

assumptions.name: No bend allowance
assumptions.value: the metal thickness and forming method are not in it

assumptions.name: Gauge, stiffening and seam type are not selected
assumptions.value: those follow the duct pressure class

standing-seam-takeoff.formula: panel count = building width / COVERAGE width, rounded up; clips per panel = panel length / clip spacing + 1; fasteners = clips x fasteners per clip; seam length = (panels - 1) x panel length.
standing-seam-takeoff.edition: The standing seam takeoff identities by name. CLIP SPACING IS NOT DETERMINED HERE: it comes from the tested assembly's rated uplift resistance against the design pressure for each roof zone, with corners and edges much closer than the field. A takeoff on a simple rectangular plane; hips, valleys, flashing, closures and trim are not counted. The panel manufacturer's tested assembly and installation instructions, the wind design for the building, and the roofing contractor govern.
standing-seam-takeoff.freeAccess: Two divisions on a coverage width and a clip spacing the reader has; no manufacturer table is reproduced.
standing-seam-takeoff.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
standing-seam-takeoff.editionNote: COVERAGE WIDTH IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS AND IT IS NOT THE PANEL WIDTH. A sixteen inch coverage panel is roll-formed from a wider sheet and the difference goes into the seam, so ordering on the sheet width comes up several panels short with the last one landing well before the rake. CLIP SPACING IS A STRUCTURAL OUTPUT rather than an installer's choice: the clips hold the roof down against uplift, and corners and edges need much closer spacing than the field. A roof clipped at a uniform field spacing is under-attached exactly where the wind is strongest, which is the pattern seen after wind events -- the field intact and the perimeter gone.

assumptions.name: Clip spacing is entered, not designed
assumptions.value: it comes from the tested assembly against the zone's design pressure
assumptions.source: the wind design for the building

assumptions.name: A simple rectangular plane
assumptions.value: hips, valleys and transitions are most of the labour and much of the material

assumptions.name: Panel gauge and profile are not selected
assumptions.value: the span and load determine them

fan-pad-evaporative-cooling.formula: pad outlet = dry bulb - saturation efficiency x (dry bulb - wet bulb); pad area = airflow / face velocity; pad-to-fan rise = sensible gain / (1.08 x airflow).
fan-pad-evaporative-cooling.edition: Customary greenhouse figures: 8 cfm per square foot of floor in summer and 250 fpm pad face velocity for cellulose. Pad manufacturer saturation data and the design wet bulb for the site govern.
fan-pad-evaporative-cooling.freeAccess: Public psychrometric relations; saturation efficiency comes from the pad manufacturer.
fan-pad-evaporative-cooling.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
fan-pad-evaporative-cooling.editionNote: The pad cannot cool below the outdoor WET BULB, so that is the climate's own limit. The crop is not a load on the cooling system but part of it: a well-watered crop returns about half the solar gain as latent heat, and an empty house roughly doubles the pad-to-fan rise.

assumptions.name: Gradient
assumptions.value: the crop gets a gradient, not pad-end air -- a uniform crop grown in two climates

assumptions.name: Latent fraction
assumptions.value: entered; it varies with crop, stage, and how well watered the crop is

grow-light-fixture-count.formula: photons required = target PPFD x area in square metres; fixtures = required / (fixture PPF x on-target fraction), rounded up; efficacy = PPF / input watts; heat = connected watts x 3.412 Btu/h.
grow-light-fixture-count.edition: The fixture manufacturer's PPF rating and a photometric layout govern the actual distribution.
grow-light-fixture-count.freeAccess: Public arithmetic; PPF ratings are published by fixture manufacturers.
grow-light-fixture-count.governance: Estimate. AHJ and licensed professional govern.
grow-light-fixture-count.editionNote: The on-target fraction is a number most lighting plans never state and it decides the order quantity by itself. Every connected watt arrives as heat -- a credit in December and a cooling load in March -- which makes lighting and ventilation one control decision rather than two.

assumptions.name: On-target fraction
assumptions.value: entered; the share of emitted photons landing on the crop rather than the aisle or wall

assumptions.name: Distribution
assumptions.value: uniform average assumed; a real layout has a distribution the count does not capture

lift-station-outage-storage.formula: wet well = plan area x (overflow elevation - high-alarm elevation) x 1728/231 gal; sewer = 3 pi d_in^2 / 231 (= 0.0408 d^2) gal/ft x length; time to overflow = storage / inflow; response = detection + travel + hookup; shortfall = inflow x response - storage when positive; haul loads = ceil((inflow x outage - storage) / truck gallons).
lift-station-outage-storage.edition: Great Lakes-Upper Mississippi River Board, Recommended Standards for Wastewater Facilities (Ten States Standards), Sections 47.1, 47.2, and 47.433, by name, as the emergency-storage requirement; the arithmetic is a mass balance. The state regulatory agency and the utility's emergency response plan govern.
lift-station-outage-storage.freeAccess: The Ten States Standards are free to read; the requirement is named, not reproduced, and the storage and time are a mass balance on the user's dimensions and inflow.
lift-station-outage-storage.governance: Estimate. Operator of record and primacy agency govern.
lift-station-outage-storage.editionNote: A lift station without power is a tank with a fixed volume and an inflow that does not stop. Everything between the high-level alarm and the lowest point where sewage escapes is emergency storage, and the incoming gravity sewer adds to it as it surcharges -- often most of it. The Ten States Standards require the storage to cover detection plus the transport and connection of portable generating equipment, and in a regional outage the response is much longer than people guess. The shortfall is what ends up in basements. When no generator is coming, pump-and-haul loads net of storage show why a portable pump connection is worth its cost.

assumptions.name: Wet-weather inflow
assumptions.value: the inflow during the storm that caused the outage, not the dry-weather average

assumptions.name: Full-pipe sewer storage
assumptions.value: the gravity line below the overflow elevation taken full, ignoring slope -- an upper bound

assumptions.name: Lowest escape point governs
assumptions.value: the wet-well overflow, a manhole rim, or the lowest basement drain on the line, whichever is lowest

picket-anchor-soil.formula: design load per picket from the FOG table (1 in x 48 in pin: 500 / 750 / 1,000 lb in poor / average / good cohesive soil, 50 / 55 / 63 lb in loose / medium / dense cohesionless; 3 in pin: 1,000 / 1,500 / 2,000 and 150 / 180 / 190 lb), driven 36 in; count = ceil(required force / design load); group = count x design load; embedment under 36 in and cohesionless soil flagged.
picket-anchor-soil.edition: USACE US&R Structures Specialist Field Operations Guide (2006), Approximate Design Load of Pickets (Pins) in Soils, based on FHWA-IP-84-11, Handbook on Design of Piles and Drilled Shafts Under Lateral Load (1984), at about 50% of capacity; USACE US&R Shoring Operations Guide, Ed. 5.0 (2021), minimum picket 1 in x 36 in driven 24 in.
picket-anchor-soil.freeAccess: A table lookup from a federal field guide and a ceiling division.
picket-anchor-soil.governance: Estimate. Head rigger and manufacturer working-load-limit charts govern. Inspect every piece of hardware before the show.
picket-anchor-soil.editionNote: A driven picket resists a sideways pull by bearing on the soil in front of it, so the soil sets the load, and the published loads span a factor of twenty between good clay and loose sand. Pickets are a clay-and-firm-ground method; in granular soil the count becomes absurd -- 28 pickets for a 1,520 lb raker force in medium sand -- and the answer is a deadman, a buried timber, or a connection to paving. The table assumes a 48 in picket driven 36 in; the 2021 SOG permits a 1 in x 36 in picket driven 24 in for its prescribed standard patterns (6 per raker in cohesive soil, 3 into paving), which does not earn the tabulated load, so a shorter embedment is flagged rather than scaled. The 2011 DHS field guide's pattern is 4 pickets per raker in soil. Group spacing is assumed wide enough that pickets do not share a soil wedge.

assumptions.name: Soil governs, not steel
assumptions.value: a 1 in picket holds 1,000 lb in good cohesive soil and 50 lb in loose sand
assumptions.source: USACE US&R Structures Specialist FOG (2006), after FHWA-IP-84-11

assumptions.name: Table basis is 36 in of embedment
assumptions.value: a shallower picket does not earn the tabulated load and is flagged

assumptions.name: Design load is about half of capacity
assumptions.value: about 50% of the lateral capacity from the FHWA handbook
